title: Nuclei
seo_title: Nuclei Class 12 Physics Worksheet with Answers (NCERT Chapter 13)
standard_text: Composition and size of nucleus, nuclear force. Mass-energy relation, mass defect; binding energy per nucleon and its variation with mass number; nuclear fission, nuclear fusion.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 12 Physics worksheets for NCERT Chapter 13 Nuclei: composition and size of nuclei, nuclear force, mass defect, binding energy, E = mc², fission and fusion. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: R = R₀A^(1/3); nuclear density is the same for all nuclei.
body_html:
How to think about it

A nucleus has Z protons and A − Z neutrons, held by the strong, short-range nuclear force. Its radius is R = R₀A1/3 with R₀ = 1.2 fm, so all nuclei have about the same density.

The mass of a nucleus is less than the mass of its separate nucleons; this mass defect Δm appears as binding energy Δm × 931.5 MeV. Binding energy per nucleon peaks near iron-56, so heavy nuclei release energy by fission and light nuclei by fusion.

Example

¹²⁶⁸Pb? Neutrons in ²⁰⁶₈₂Pb?

206 − 82

Answer: 124

Example

Δm = 0.03 u. BE?

0.03 × 931.5

Answer: 27.9 MeV

Common mistakes

  • Forgetting to multiply by 931.5.
  • Saying fusion splits nuclei.
  • Using A instead of A1/3 for the radius.

faq.a: The energy needed to separate a nucleus into its protons and neutrons; it equals the mass defect × c².

faq.q: Why do both fission and fusion release energy?
faq.a: In both, the products have a higher binding energy per nucleon than the starting nuclei.
